title: Rapid, Enzymatic Methods for Amplification of Minimal, Linear Templates for Protein Prototyping using Cell-Free Systems
protocol: Design the gene fragment.
Determine the desired gene to be expressed.
Obtain the amino acid sequence or genetic sequence if it has been expressed in E. coli.
Perform codon optimization for E. coli using standard vendor tools if starting with an amino acid sequence.
Ensure the optimized sequence has no HindIII restriction sites (AAGCTT).
Continue optimizing until there is no longer a HindIII site.
Copy the optimized sequence and paste it into the provided template for Supplementary Sequence #1 where indicated.
Use Supplementary Sequence #1 as is if expressing sfGFP.
Use Supplementary Sequence #2 as is if expressing subtilisin.
Order the minimal template and necessary primers from a preferred DNA synthesis service.
Centrifuge the tube containing the gene fragment (300 x g for 5 s) to collect the DNA pellet at the bottom.
Add double distilled water (ddH2O) to make a final concentration of 10 ng/μL of DNA template.
Vortex the solution on a medium setting for 5-10 s.
Dissolve the entire pellet by incubating at 50 °C for 20 min.
Briefly vortex again.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 5 s to collect the solution at the bottom of the tube.
Store the resuspended DNA at -20 °C or use in PCR.
Prepare a 100 µM primer stock by resuspending primers in nuclease-free water.
Determine the amount of ddH2O to add by multiplying the number of nanomoles of lyophilized primer by 10.
Add the calculated volume of ddH2O and vortex the solution.
Store the primer stock solutions at -20 °C.
Decide which PCR kit is right for the gene of interest.
Perform PCR amplification as necessary to preserve initial gene fragment or allow comparative studies.
Create 10 µM working solutions from 100 µM stocks.
Program the thermal cycler according to the kit manufacturer's protocols.
Set initial denaturation at 94 °C for 30 s.
Conduct 30 cycles of denaturing at 94 °C for 30 s, primer annealing at 45 °C for 30 s, and extension at 68 °C for 60 s.
Perform a final extension at 68 °C for 5 min.
Maintain the reaction at 10 °C indefinitely.
Thaw dNTPs if performing PCR and vortex them.
Use the PCR buffer provided in the kit.
Combine all kit components in a single PCR tube as directed by the manufacturer's protocol.
Add 1 µL of resuspended DNA stock to the PCR mixture.
Gently homogenize the mixture by vortexing on medium setting for 5-10 seconds.
Alternatively, pipette half the volume up and down 10-20 times to vortex.
Perform the PCR reaction.
If the PCR protocol did not include a final cooling step, allow the reaction to cool for 5 minutes at 10 °C before removing.
Purify the reaction using a PCR clean-up kit following the vendor's instructions.
In a 1.5 mL tube, add DNA binding buffer and PCR sample at a ratio of 5:1, respectively.
Transfer this mixture to the spin column and centrifuge at 16,000 x g for 1 minute.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 200 µL of DNA wash buffer to the column and incubate at room temperature for 1 minute.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 16,000 x g and discard the flow-through.
Repeat steps involving adding DNA wash buffer and centrifuging without the 1-minute incubation step.
Centrifuge for an additional 1-2 minutes at 16,000 x g to remove any remaining buffer.
Elute the DNA in 46 µL of ddH2O.
Quantify the purified DNA using a spectrophotometer.
Store the purified DNA at -20 °C or proceed to the next step.
Digest the DNA to prepare the template for circularization.
This will remove the primer sequences and create sticky ends at both the 5' and 3' ends of the template.
Reattach these ends via ligation reaction.
Combine 5 μL of the necessary buffer, 20 U of HindIII, and 45 μL of purified DNA in a PCR tube.
Gently homogenize this mixture with a pipette.
Incubate the mixture in a thermal cycler for 15 min at 37 °C.
Heat inactivate HindIII by incubating for 20 min at 80 °C.
Allow the reaction to cool to 10 °C before removing to drive condensation to the bottom of the tube.
Add 5 μL of T4 ligase buffer and 800 U of T4 ligase to the newly digested DNA.
Gently homogenize this mixture with a pipette.
Incubate the mixture for 1 h at 25 °C to perform the circularization reaction.
Purify the reaction using a PCR clean-up kit following the vendor's instructions.
Quantify the DNA using a spectrophotometer.
Combine 20 μL of sample buffer, 20 μL of reaction buffer, 0.8 μL of enzyme, and 1 μL of circular expression template (CET).
Homogenize the mixture with a pipette.
Aliquot 10 μL of the mixture into four separate tubes.
Incubate at 30 °C for 4-18 h.
Heat inactivate the enzyme by incubating at 65 °C for 10 min.
Reduce the temperature to 12 °C for 5 min.
Dilute the resulting solution by adding 15 μL of ddH2O to each tube.
Combine all tubes and add directly to a cell-free reaction.
If desired, use a PCR clean-up kit to purify the product.
Elute the purified product in 36 μL of ddH2O to quantify.
Combine energy buffer, extract, and RCA template for cell-free expression.

Use PANOx-SP energy buffer containing specified concentrations of ATP, GMP, UMP, CMP, phosphoenolpyruvate, potassium glutamate, ammonium glutamate, magnesium glutamate, spermidine, putrescine, folinic acid, E. coli tRNA mixture, unlabeled amino acids, NAD, Coenzyme A (CoA), potassium oxalate, HEPES-KOH buffer, and E. coli extract.
Dilute the solution to the final desired volume with ddH2O.
Mix the solution thoroughly by pipetting half of the solution volume up and down 10-20 times.
Prepare a plate reader for reading at the desired excitation/emission if expressing a fluorescent protein such as sfGFP.
Aliquot 60 µL of H2O into the wells bordering an empty sample well in a 384-well plate to maintain humidity and reduce edge effect.
Transfer the reaction mixture in 15 μL aliquots to the desired wells in the microtiter plate.
Seal the plate with a colorless sealing film to maintain humidity and prevent evaporation.
Place the sealed plate in the plate reader and allow the reaction to complete.
If expressing a protein that does not have the capability of being monitored live, use another temperature-controlled apparatus such as a thermoblock to incubate the plate.
Prepare a 10 µM stock solution of N-succinyl-Ala-Ala-Pro-Phe p-nitroanilide in dimethylformamide (DMF).
Set a plate reader to measure absorbance at 410 nm every 20 s for 10 min while maintaining a temperature of 25 °C.
Aliquot 94 µL of ddH2O and 1 µL of N-succinyl-Ala-Ala-Pro-Phe p-nitroanilide into a flat bottom, colorless 96-well plate.
Add 5 µL of the finished cell-free reaction to the plate.
Read using a plate reader set to measure absorbance at 410 nm every 20 s for 10 min while maintaining a temperature of 25 °C.
